assembly.sourceCondition: The legacy WornPathA box spans x=0.30..4.70 m and z=-10.05..-1.55 m while DanchiPlaza spans x=-20..4 m from z=-5.50 m onward. The higher plaza hides most of the soil top after z=-5.50 but leaves a narrow east strip visible outside x=4.0; meanwhile the two legacy 0.60 m-pitch edging runs continue to z=-1.656 m. This produces a contradictory partly-buried rectangular path and curb continuation instead of a deliberate plaza-mouth termination.
components: coarse WornPathA gameplay/collision substrate retained but renderer suppressed
authored visible compacted-soil path surface ending at the plaza boundary
two modular precast concrete edging runs retained only through the last whole module before the plaza
356 mm open transition mouth between the final curb modules and plaza edge
assembly.manufacture: The compacted pedestrian path is represented by an authored top surface rather than the vertical walls of a Unity box. Individual precast concrete edging blocks remain modular manufactured units on prepared bedding/subbase. Buried bedding is represented by the installation datum and metadata rather than exposed decorative geometry.
assembly.mounting: Each retained edging block is embedded 10 mm below the nominal compacted-soil top and stands approximately 70 mm above it. The two runs straddle the soil path with an approximately 5 mm inner interface gap. The curbs terminate on the last whole module before the plaza. Over the final 356 mm the visible soil mouth rises gradually toward the paving and narrows to meet the plaza corner without extending beneath the paved field.
assembly.interfaces: soil-to-curb inner seams, grass-to-curb outer faces, modular block joints, the open transition mouth, and a 1 mm below-paving terminal soil edge at z=-5.500 m
assembly.orientation: long axis north-south; pedestrian flow approaches the plaza from negative Z toward positive Z
assembly.exposure: soil and curb tops are sun/rain exposed; curb lower faces receive soil splash; inner seams retain fine sediment; path center receives foot compaction and the open mouth receives turning/cross-traffic wear
assembly.aging: Weathering is cause-based: curb lower-face splash, joint sediment, modest top-edge wear and path-center compaction may occur. No random crack field, painted contact shadow or identical copied stain is allowed.
assembly.geometryVsMaterial: Visible path outline/elevation, curb dimensions/chamfer/module spacing, path-to-curb gap, termination setback and paved/soil height relationship are geometry. Soil grain, aggregate, micro-roughness, subtle color variation, moisture response and UV aging belong to the material/shader.
assembly.periodAuthenticity: A modest compacted shortcut with modular concrete edging beside a residential plaza is treated as period-plausible fallback infrastructure. No claim is made that these exact dimensions reproduce a specific housing estate or historical product.

curbMaterial.microstructure: dense precast cement paste with small aggregate; edge response comes from physical chamfer rather than painted highlights
curbMaterial.wetResponse: if a later wet benchmark is authored, albedo may darken and roughness may fall locally according to real exposure; the current dry midsummer benchmark remains dry
curbMaterial.uvAging: small warm/gray drift and modest upper-face fade only; no repeated identical dirt stamp
curbMaterial.angularFresnelResponse: rough dielectric F0 near 0.04 with broad grazing lift; never metallic or mirror-like

soilMaterial.microstructure: compacted mineral fines and small grit; no baked foot shadow or directional highlight
soilMaterial.uvAging: sun-exposed dry mineral color may drift modestly; pedestrian compaction changes roughness/relief by context rather than copied stain decals
soilMaterial.angularFresnelResponse: very rough dielectric response with weak broad grazing lift and no metallic sparkle

lodPolicy.lod0: retain the authored compacted-soil surface plus seven whole authored chamfered curb modules per side and their physical joints
lodPolicy.lod1: retain the same installed path/curb silhouette; no geometry-changing cutover is permitted until rendered evidence proves a cheaper representation does not pop
lodPolicy.lod2: retain the same installed path/curb silhouette because the corrected assembly is small relative to the benchmark and avoids an unverified path-width/curb transition
lodPolicy.lod3: retain the same installed path/curb silhouette; distance optimization may be introduced only with temporal evidence proving no visible pop
lodPolicy.transitionPolicy: The generated fallback intentionally spends a small fixed renderer cost to eliminate an unverified LOD shape change. Any future authored replacement must provide explicit LOD0/1/2/3 evidence.

researchBasis.source: Yokohama City park/green-space standard drawings, current reference edition
researchBasis.referenceUse: Installation principle only: modular concrete edging/curb blocks are placed on mortar/base layers and treated as discrete manufactured units. Current drawings show common 600 mm modules; exact present-day joint/base dimensions are not asserted as circa-2000 site facts.

evidencePlan: hero/ground_contact 100% crop: confirm the authored soil surface ends cleanly at the plaza instead of continuing as a primitive rectangular strip beneath/alongside paving
hero or oblique full frame: confirm no parallel curb rails continue into the paved field and the open mouth reads as a pedestrian connection rather than a cut-off asset
oblique/vegetation_grounding 100% crop where visible: confirm final curb modules have manufactured end faces, believable soil/grass contact and no floating edge
grazing/material_grazing if the path mouth enters frame: verify rough dielectric concrete and soil, physical curb chamfer, stable metric texture scale and no painted highlight
temporal evidence: confirm the coarse WornPathA renderer and suppressed legacy curb modules never reappear and no silhouette/texture shimmer appears
criticalFailPrevention: no active legacy curb geometry may project into the DanchiPlaza paved field
no visible coarse WornPathA Unity-box renderer may survive in benchmark framing
no visible authored soil surface may continue beyond the plaza edge or leave the legacy 0.70 m east strip
no retained curb renderer or replacement soil surface may use Unity primitive render geometry
no metallic/specularly impossible curb or soil material
no claim of visual quality without actual rendered evidence
